answer_text:
The base region is the disk

\[
x^2+y^2\le 2x \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (x-1)^2+y^2\le 1.
\]

Using polar coordinates \(x=r\cos\theta,\;y=r\sin\theta\),

\[
r^2=2r\cos\theta \implies r=2\cos\theta.
\]

Since \(r\ge 0\), we need \(\cos\theta\ge 0\), so the correct \(\theta\)-limits are

\[
-\frac{\pi}{2}\le \theta\le \frac{\pi}{2}.
\]

The plane is

\[
3x+4y+z=12 \implies z=12-3x-4y,
\]

so the \(z\)-limits are

\[
0\le z\le 12-3r\cos\theta-4r\sin\theta.
\]

Thus the volume is

\[
V=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\int_0^{2\cos\theta}
\int_0^{12-3r\cos\theta-4r\sin\theta} r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta.
\]

Integrating in \(z\),

\[
V=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\int_0^{2\cos\theta}
\left(12-3r\cos\theta-4r\sin\theta\right)r\,dr\,d\theta.
\]

Compute the inner integral:

\[
\int_0^{2\cos\theta}\left(12r-3r^2\cos\theta-4r^3\sin\theta\right)dr
=24\cos^2\theta-8\cos^4\theta-16\sin\theta\cos^4\theta.
\]

Therefore,

\[
V=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}
\left(24\cos^2\theta-8\cos^4\theta-16\sin\theta\cos^4\theta\right)d\theta.
\]

Using

\[
\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac{\pi}{2},
\qquad
\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^4\theta\,d\theta=\frac{3\pi}{8},
\]

and the last term integrates to \(0\) by symmetry,

\[
V=24\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-8\left(\frac{3\pi}{8}\right)
=12\pi-3\pi=9\pi.
\]

\[
\boxed{9\pi}
\]
